name: Data Warehousing
certifications: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate (DP-700)

beginner.summary: For analysts, developers and BI staff who know basic SQL and are new to data warehousing. Covers OLTP versus OLAP, warehouse layers, facts, dimensions and grain, star and snowflake schemas, surrogate keys and the date dimension, slowly changing dimensions Types 0 to 2, loading with SQL, additivity, conformed dimensions, analytical SQL and window functions, columnar storage, incremental loads, data quality checks, marts and BI access, documentation, query plans and a retail star schema capstone, using PostgreSQL and DuckDB.
prerequisites: Can write SELECT queries with joins, GROUP BY and WHERE in any SQL dialect
Uses a terminal and can install software or run Docker containers on a laptop
Understands basic relational concepts such as tables, primary keys and foreign keys
outcomes: Design and build a star schema from a stated grain with surrogate keys, SCD2 and a date dimension
Load and reconcile dimensions and facts with idempotent SQL and watermark-based incremental loads
Write analytical SQL with ROLLUP, window functions and read query plans to fix simple slowness
Expose a governed mart to a BI tool through views and a read-only role

Source systems: ERP, CRM, e-commerce, flat files and SaaS APIs
Batch refresh versus near-real-time loading
Roles on a warehouse team: architect, data engineer, analytics engineer and data steward
The two founding schools: Kimball bottom-up and Inmon top-down
Success measures: trusted numbers, refresh latency, query time and adoption
days.lab_task: In PostgreSQL create schema oltp with customers (500 rows) and orders (200000 rows) using INSERT ... SELECT FROM generate_series. Run a monthly revenue by region report with \timing and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS). Then UPDATE customer 7 to region 'West', re-run the report and record how past months changed.
days.deliverable: One-page memo with the report timings, the plan and a before-and-after table showing history rewritten
checks: Run the monthly revenue report under EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
Plan shows a Seq Scan on orders and an Execution Time in milliseconds
Plan text saved to a file
UPDATE oltp.customers SET region='West' WHERE customer_id=7, then re-run the report
Revenue of customer 7 moves from the old region to West for every past month, proving the OLTP model keeps no history
Two result sets side by side
objectives: Contrast OLTP and OLAP workloads with measured evidence
State the four properties of a data warehouse
Explain why operational databases rewrite history and why a warehouse must not

intermediate.summary: For data engineers and analytics engineers who have built a basic star schema. Covers requirements gathering, dimension patterns, hierarchies and bridge tables, advanced SCD types, snapshot and factless facts, late-arriving data, currency handling, ELT layering, CDC with MERGE, Inmon and Data Vault 2.0 with PIT tables, MPP distribution and skew, partitioning, materialised aggregates, semantic layers, data quality frameworks, orchestration and backfills, and a multi-process warehouse capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed a star schema with fact and dimension tables and can write window functions
Can script SQL loads with psql or a similar client and use Git
Understands incremental loading, surrogate keys and Type 2 history
outcomes: Model complex requirements with hierarchies, bridges, snapshot facts and late-arriving data
Build ELT pipelines with CDC, MERGE, Data Vault 2.0 loads and information marts
Tune storage layout using partitioning, distribution and materialised aggregates and prove the gain
Govern metrics with a semantic layer, quality tests and parameterised backfills

advanced.summary: For senior engineers and architects who own warehouse platforms. Covers enterprise architecture choices, open table formats, optimiser statistics, workload management, tuning at billions of rows, FinOps, row-level security and masking, governance and lineage, privacy and erasure, bitemporal modelling, streaming ingestion, data contracts and sharing, a two-day vendor-neutral comparison of Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift and Fabric, migration reconciliation, CI/CD, observability, disaster recovery, AI-assisted analytics and a design-review capstone.
prerequisites: Has delivered at least one production warehouse or mart with incremental loads and quality checks
Reads query plans and understands partitioning, distribution and SCD patterns
Is comfortable with Python or shell scripting, Docker and a CI system
outcomes: Choose and defend an enterprise warehouse architecture and platform using weighted evidence
Secure, govern and make the warehouse privacy-compliant with row policies, masking, lineage and erasure
Run the warehouse reliably with workload isolation, FinOps, observability, CI/CD and tested recovery
Plan and reconcile a legacy migration and evaluate AI-assisted analytics safely
